scope: Theorem 3.1 (Signed excess) of the manuscript “Almost-everywhere regularity of stationary integral varifolds” (preprints/Almost-everywhere-regularity-of-stationary-integral-varifolds-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 346 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f12bd8f9ace9a350), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive integer Q and κ > 0. Work in the interior normal-cylinder setting of Section 2, with base coordinates scaled by a physical radius l so that B4 is available. Suppose τ(B4) ≤ d = e−T , l + sup |zphys| ≤ e−κT . (3.3) The supremum is over the restricted support above the available chart. The statement also holds after an interior rescaling in the inherited frames of Theorem 2.10, provided in the curved case the second smallness condition is imposed on the inherited parameter γ from (2.6). There are a constant CQ and a threshold T0, depending only on the stated fixed data, such that for T ≥ T0, ∫ w (L − CQΛ) ≤ e−FQ(T) d (3.4) whenever w is supported in B1, 0 ≤ w ≤ 1, and Lip w ≤ 1. For a flat reference plane, take Λ = 0 and omit the second condition in (3.3); constant sheet offsets need not be bounded.
